messages:
maya: quick heads-up — seeing accuracy drop on short-form QA (<=50 tokens) when serving weight-only INT8 with bitsandbytes. eval slice=short_answers_small. baseline fp16 acc=91.8 -> bnb-int8 acc=86.4. Anyone seen this?

dmitri: can you paste the exact slice numbers, model variant, and quant config?

maya: model=voyager-13b, quant=weight-only 8bit via bitsandbytes 0.39 (bnb4), llm.int8 mode not used. eval: 1k examples, seeds=3. metrics: acc fp16=91.8, bnb-int8=86.4, llmint8(py)=89.2. p50 token latency (steady) fp16=7ms, bnb-int8=12ms, coldstart p50 bnb-int8 spike to ~28ms for first 10 requests. attached small log snippet.

sarah: interesting — short prompts are sensitive to small activation changes and kv-cache warming. weight-only quant can alter activation scale in output layers. did you try warmup or continuous-batching?

maya: quick warmup (5 synthetic prompts) reduced the cold p50 to ~15ms and bumped bnb-int8 acc to 89.5, but still below fp16. quality gap persists on factual short answers (yes/no and numeric).

kevin: worth comparing with the llm.int8 path (HF native int8) — we've seen better per-layer preservation there. also run a per-layer sensitivity pass (small GPTQ-style MSE or KL) to find the few layers causing majority of error.

quant-bot: eval-run finished: slice=short_answers_small, examples=1000, baseline_fp16 acc=91.8, bnb-int8 acc=86.4, llmint8 acc=89.2, delta_vs_fp16: bnb=-5.4, llm=-2.6, notes="bnb has bigger shortform degradation". dashboard: https://redwood-evals/shortform/182900

sarah: operational suggestion: add runtime fallback for seq_len<=50 to route to fp16 or llmint8 variant until we have a stable quant profile. example rollout snippet: 

```
route:
  - condition: request.seq_len <= 50 and model_variant == \"bnb-int8\"
    action: fallback_to: \"fp16-voyager-13b\"
    reason: shortform_quality_drop
```

maya: plan: run controlled bakeoff tomorrow — 3k short QAs across 3 seeds comparing bnb-int8, llmint8(py), and fp16. collect accuracy, tokenized cost, GPU utilization, and coldstart tail latency. tagging @kevin @dmitri to help with layer sensitivity scripts.

dmitri: please also capture per-layer activation ranges and max-quantization-error heatmap. if llmint8 gives quality+cost win we can consider it default for shortform routes.

ops-bot: scheduled job queued: shortform-8bit-bakeoff id=1829001245, owner=maya, window=2h, priority=high.

maya: thanks — I'll post results here once finished :thumbsup:
